h.strategy: After listing and negating default assumptions, keep only the negations that a general mechanism supports. Candidate mechanisms: parent quality (strong parents leave little room to improve and have more to lose), redundancy (duplicate or similar options dilute each other's contribution), and bottlenecks (an option matters little when it is not on the path to the output, however strong it is). Prefer predictions in which a usually helpful edit becomes neutral or harmful in a common context, or a usually harmful edit becomes harmless. Avoid conditions that only a few parents satisfy. Spread hypotheses across different edited fields and condition fields. Give at least four 'lower' predictions where the intuitive guess would be 'higher'.

hyps.why: A strong parallel conv path into the output makes the extra direct conv redundant.
With a strong direct conv path already present, a conv on edge 5 adds little and dilutes.
Removing edge 4 leaves node 1 only a longer route to the output, so edge 0's conv matters less.
Node 2 reaches the output only through edge 5, so with it removed edge 1's conv is off the output path.
Edge 2 feeds only node 2, which is disconnected from the output when edge 5 is none.
Node 1 receives no input when edge 0 is none, so a conv on edge 4 processes nothing.
Replacing a missing direct edge with a conv gains far more than upgrading an existing op.
Dropping a weak pooling op costs little, whereas dropping a conv or skip on the direct edge costs a lot.
A strong parent with a direct 3x3 conv leaves little room for another conv path to improve accuracy.
Two skip paths into node 2 are redundant, so the second adds less than it would after a weaker op.
